On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an order directing federal agencies not to recognize U.S. citizenship for certain children born in the United States. It applied when the mother was unlawfully present, or lawfully but temporarily present, and the father was neither a U.S. citizen nor a lawful permanent resident. It expressly did not affect children of lawful permanent residents. The order was scheduled to apply to births more than 30 days later. Reuters reports that a federal judge in Maryland issued a class-action injunction on August 7, 2025, the fourth court to block the policy nationwide. Reuters also describes earlier court orders and the Supreme Court’s June 27, 2025 decision limiting universal injunctions without deciding the order’s constitutionality.
